# A column can be generated by the database

`Column` has an optional flag, `generated`, meaning the database produces the value. It is allowed on `integer`, `bigint` and `uuid`. The dialect decides how it is written: in PostgreSQL an integer or bigint becomes `GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY` and a uuid gets `DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()`, placed after `NOT NULL`.

For the integer, `GENERATED BY DEFAULT` was chosen over `GENERATED ALWAYS` (which rejects an explicit id on insert, a problem when importing data) and over `serial` (the old form, discouraged). For the uuid, a default was chosen over leaving it bare, because a generated uuid id that nobody fills is of no use; `gen_random_uuid()` is built into PostgreSQL 13 and later, and earlier versions need the `pgcrypto` extension.

## Consequences

**Projects saved before this keep working.** The flag is optional and absent means false, so nothing was migrated and `formatVersion` did not change. `parseProject` accepts it absent or boolean and rejects anything else, with its path.

**A generated column of another type is a draft problem, not a file error.** It loads, `validate` reports `generated-unsupported-type`, and the DDL generator refuses the schema. The editing UI clears the flag when the user changes the type, so it only arises in a hand-edited file.

**It is not a general `DEFAULT`.** Only generation is modeled. A default value for any column is still out of scope.

**The clause belongs to the dialect.** `Dialect.generatedClause(type)` returns the text or `null`; another dialect can spell it its own way.


## Amendment: timestamp

A `timestamp` column can also be generated. The PostgreSQL dialect writes it as `DEFAULT now()` on a `timestamptz` column (the logical `timestamp` already maps to `timestamptz`, which stores UTC). It does not imply `NOT NULL`. A trigger to refresh `updated_at` on update is out of scope.
